gate_contract.comment: Gate contract: a flat map from each arm THIS paper compares to the shell command that produces it. The paper's headline comparison (Goodfellow et al. 2015, tex:492-494) is clean maxout training ('baseline') vs FGSM adversarial training ('adversarial', Algorithm B, eps=0.25, alpha=0.5). Each command prints EXACTLY one line `FINAL <arm name>=<clean test accuracy>`; run_all_arms.sh runs both and the gate pairs each line to its arm by name. arms.json holds ONLY the runnable arms; this section holds the explanatory notes that previously lived as '_'-prefixed keys in arms.json (removed because the gate requires a FINAL line for every key).
gate_contract.degeneracy: run_experiment.py --lambda 0 (arm 'adversarial' at its no-op) must print the SAME accuracy VALUE as --baseline (arm 'baseline'); tested by tests/test_degeneracy.py
gate_contract.environment_note: Commands rely on run_all_arms.sh / smoke.sh exporting OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 and MKL_NUM_THREADS=4 (PyTorch's default thread pool over-spawns on multi-core CPUs, a ~7x slowdown). The CLI itself leaves threading to the environment.
gate_contract.paper: Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples (Goodfellow, Shlens, Szegedy; ICLR 2015; arXiv:1412.6572v3)

paper_target.note: adversarial training should reduce clean test error vs baseline (i.e. raise clean test accuracy). At the degeneracy-valid harness scale (dropout off, fixed SGD steps) we reproduce the DIRECTION: adversarial >= baseline. The paper's exact 0.94%->0.84% magnitudes require full convergence with dropout + early stopping (see experiments/m4_adversarial.py, results/m4_adversarial.json).

gate_contract.value_definition: clean test accuracy = mean(argmax logits == y) over the 10k MNIST test set (printed as FINAL <arm>=<value>)

graded_harness.baseline_arm: --baseline: identical maxout MLP trained on the clean cost only
graded_harness.degeneracy_requirement: --lambda 0 and --baseline must print bit-identical FINAL lines (eps=0 => x_tilde==x => J~==J; dropout off by default in the harness); tested by tests/test_degeneracy.py
graded_harness.method_arm: --lambda EPS (default eps=0.25): FGSM adversarial training (Algorithm B, J~ = alpha*J + (1-alpha)*J(x+eps*sign(grad_x J)), alpha=0.5 per tex:488); runs by default including at eps=0
graded_harness.output_contract: exactly one stdout line matching /^FINAL (baseline|adversarial)=[0-9.]+$/ where the arm name matches the keys in arms.json; <value> is the clean test accuracy. All other output goes to stderr.

metric_definitions.error_rate: fraction of ALL evaluated examples misclassified = mean(argmax logits != y); over all examples, not only originally-correct ones (SPEC.md §6 item 13)
metric_definitions.mean_confidence_on_errors: softmax probability of the PREDICTED class, averaged over the misclassified subset only (SPEC.md §6 item 14; tex:333-341, 521-523, 600-604)
metric_definitions.no_clipping: FGSM-perturbed inputs are never clipped back to [0,1] (SPEC.md §6 item 12; tex:235,309)
metric_definitions.rubbish_error_rate: fraction of N(0,I_F) samples with max_k p(y=k|x) > 0.5 (tex:905-906); sigmoid-top variant: any per-class sigmoid > 0.5
